author: agent
text:
DEFECT, measured 2026-08-16 on memway's own map: UNIQUENESS IS BEING TREATED AS CERTAINTY, and it hands ~23% of call edges to the wrong target at high confidence.

`conf, how = 0.95, "exact"` is set the moment ix.resolve() returns anything, before anything checks HOW it resolved. resolve() falls back to bare-name matching, so a short name with exactly ONE definition anywhere in the repo becomes the target for every call of that name - including calls the repo never defines, i.e. stdlib and builtin methods.

Measured: 369 of 1627 call edges (23%) land on an entity whose short name is a stdlib/builtin method. Two of them absorb 295 edges between them - 18% of every call edge in the map:

  tests.test_console.get                                     159 incoming
  tests.test_version...test_editable_marker...D.read_text    136 incoming

The second is a one-line stub class D defined INSIDE a test function. Every `p.read_text()` in the package - access_cache.load_json_cached, cli._is_editable, cli.plan_rules_write - is attributed to it, at confidence 0.95, labelled "exact". `get` collects every `dict.get()` in the repo including from docs/examples.

Two consequences. Visually it is why the graph has a hairball: two meaningless nodes act as magnets for a fifth of all edges. Analytically it is worse - fan_in on those stubs is fiction, and the blast radius of anything that reaches them is inflated by hundreds of false paths.

The D11b tiebreak (prefer production over tests when a bare name is ambiguous) cannot help here: it only fires when there is competition, and these names have exactly one definition. No competition is being read as high confidence when it is the case that most deserves suspicion.

Wanted: a bare-name fallback must not score "exact". Either drop to the low-confidence tier (<0.7, which the grounding block already surfaces and warns about), or refuse to resolve a receiver-method call whose name is defined only inside a test scope or a function-local class. Do not special-case a list of stdlib names - the rule is about HOW it resolved, not about which names Python happens to ship.

author: cli
text: SUPERSEDES the DEFECT note below. Fixed in 0.54.3; that note is history - read it for the measurements, not for what this code does. What holds now: _unreachable_target rejects three things a bare name can never legally be. (1) FUNCTION-LOCAL targets: a class or def inside a function body cannot be named from outside it. (2) AN ATTRIBUTE CALL IS NOT A MODULE-LEVEL FUNCTION: d.get(x) cannot be 'def get' at module scope - RawEdge.via_attr carries the fact the parser used to discard, which is why PARSE_SCHEMA_VERSION went 4 to 5. (3) PRODUCTION CODE DOES NOT CALL TEST HELPERS. All three are facts about scope, deliberately not a list of stdlib names - such a list is endless, language-specific, and wrong the moment a repo legitimately defines get. Result here: read_text 136->0 incoming, get 159->19, 850 edges dropped. THE THING THAT WILL BITE NEXT: FOUR tiers in this method match on a short name - exact, annotated, inherited-guess, bare-name fallback. The first pass guarded two and the others kept feeding the same false hubs until re-measuring found them; reading the code had not. test_units_core2 now walks build() by AST and fails if ANY comprehension touching _by_short lacks a guard. Do not move the guard into resolve(): rules 2 and 3 are about the caller, which resolve() has no business knowing.

author: cli
text:
Re-stated after the imported-receiver work. The three reachability rules below still hold; two more resolution paths were closed in the same family.

(4) A CALL INTO AN IMPORTED MODULE IS QUALIFIED, NOT GUESSED. The parser now emits subprocess.run instead of a bare run when the receiver is a name bound by an import. Qualifying rather than dropping is deliberate: query.summary() has the same shape and IS ours, so it resolves properly and gets a BETTER edge, while subprocess.run resolves to nothing and correctly disappears.

(5) A DOTTED REF IS NOT GUESSED WHEN ITS PREFIX IS UNKNOWN. Qualifying in the parser was only half the fix - the inherited-guess tier took the dotted ref, threw the prefix away and matched the last segment against every entity, putting the edge back exactly where it had been removed. That tier exists for inheritance dispatch, where the prefix always names a class this repo has, so it is now gated on the prefix resolving.

Result: Harvester.run 61 -> 5 incoming (77 subprocess.run call sites stopped landing there), edges 2901 -> 2554 across the whole effort, and every top-of-fan-in entry is real code. Indexer.resolve keeps its 109 because those ARE Indexer instances - 84 ix.resolve plus variants, checked by reading the receivers.

Known gap: the inherited-guess tier is unfalsified in the TOO-TIGHT direction. The inheritance test that covers dispatch is served by the MRO tier at 0.90 and stays green with the guess tier disabled entirely, so no fixture here proves the gate is not over-restrictive.

author: agent
text:
Re-stated at 0.57.2. The reachability rules below all still hold; one more was added in the same family, and it is the same disease the ORIGINAL defect note on this coordinate named.

That note, from 2026-08-16, is titled "UNIQUENESS IS BEING TREATED AS CERTAINTY". 0.54.3 fixed it for the case where a bare name had SEVERAL definitions and the resolver picked one. The case it did not cover is the mirror: a bare name with EXACTLY ONE definition in the repo, where the real target is not in the repo at all.

(6) A BARE CALL SPELLING A LANGUAGE BUILTIN IS THE BUILTIN. prometheus declares `func (c *memChunk) len() int`, the only entity in that repo named len, so candidates() returned one, resolution was "exact", confidence 0.95, and every builtin len(x) in 727 files landed on a three-line method: 1,619 incoming call edges, 9.9% of the map's call traffic, next-highest 342. sqlalchemy is worse in kind - Options.isinstance took 1,150, BaseRow.getattr 367, Row.tuple 185. No competition read as high confidence, on precisely the coordinates that deserved suspicion.

The rule fires only when the callee is a METHOD, no receiver was written (RawEdge.bare), and the name is one the CALLER's language defines. Refusal reason: "builtin-call".

TWO THINGS NOT TO REDISCOVER.

First, the rule was originally the broader "a bare call is not a method", and that is FALSE. rich binds `add_row = items_table.add_row` and calls `add_row(...)`; a bound-method alias keeps the name, and JS destructuring does the same. It cost rich 96% -> 94% and sqlalchemy its floor within one network run.

Second, and worse hidden: when the resolver was fixed, sqlalchemy's measured recall FELL to 44% and the floor failed. The obvious response - lower the floor - would have locked the defect in as a baseline. The ORACLE was wrong: tests/test_corpus_recall.py attributed bare isinstance(x,y) to the repo method too, so tool and oracle were wrong identically and their agreement scored as 76% recall. Corrected, sqlalchemy reads 74% (denominator down 1,709) and rich reads 98%, UP from 96% - the tell that the change was a fix.

STILL OPEN and untouched: a call whose real target is outside the repo but is not a builtin. DirLocker.Lock takes 342 edges on prometheus (`mu.Lock()` on a stdlib sync.Mutex), Timer.Duration 211. Builtins were the tractable head of that distribution because the language defines the set; stdlib and dependency receivers need type information this map does not carry.
